discoveries: This session was itself launched with the pre-DEC-873 launcher's Read deny rules for (c), and the CLI turned them into OS-level read denials. That reproduces P-W2-58-1 in the test designer's own session: the code under test cannot be imported, and git sees phantom changes (` M` here, where the engineer's session saw ` D`). So a red run from this session would show ImportErrors, not the intended red reason ("the launcher still adds Read deny rules for (c) and (d)"). Policy 2 (c)'s "you may run the implementation" cannot be honoured under this launch.
risks: If this role is relaunched the same way, the next test designer hits the same stop. If someone instead goes past check (b), their red run will be red for the wrong reason (failed imports) and will look like valid evidence.
lessons: Until DEC-873's launcher change lands, a session launched by the current `gov launch` for a W2-58 role carries the OS-level read denial that the ticket is meant to remove. Running this ticket's test-designer job needs a launch whose settings have no (c) or (d) `Read` deny rules.
proposed_decisions: P-W2-58-2, on how to relaunch the W2-58 test designer so it can run the code it tests. (a) Relaunch with the (c)/(d) `Read` deny rules left out of the settings and keep the held-out (b) rules, so the guard alone refuses (c) and (d). That is DEC-873 item 2's own design, applied ahead of the fix by the lead or orchestrator. (b) Relaunch with the CLI's sandbox off for this session, keeping the guard. (c) Let this session write the cases without running them, and have the lead run the red from an unsandboxed session. Recommendation: (a), confidence high. It matches DEC-873, keeps (b)'s held-out protection and lets the test designer show a valid red itself.
